item.text: I found three event write paths and three read paths. The existing date migration provides a locking pattern to follow. I’ll use a native `FieldsMap` for new writes, keep reads compatible with legacy `Fields` rows, and add a separate migration for existing rows.

The new storage path compiles, and the available package tests pass. I’ve also made the field migration wait for the existing date migration so their batch writes cannot replace each other’s changes. Next I’ll verify JSON round trips and both row formats with focused tests.

package dynamoevents

import (
	\"encoding/json\"
	\"testing\"

	\"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/aws\"
	\"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/service/dynamodb\"
	\"github.com/stretchr/testify/require\"
)

func TestFieldsMapRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	original := []byte("'`{"empty":"","nested":{"list":[null,true,false,"",{},[],12345678901234567890,1.25]},"zero":0}`)
	item, err := marshalEventItem(event{SessionID: "session", EventIndex: 1, Fields: string(original)})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Nil(t, item["Fields"])
	require.NotNil(t, item[keyFieldsMap].M)
	require.Equal(t, "", aws.StringValue(item[keyFieldsMap].M["empty"].S))
	require.Equal(t, "12345678901234567890", aws.StringValue(item[keyFieldsMap].M["nested"].M["list"].L[6].N))

	converted, err := unmarshalEventItem(item)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	want, err := parseFields(original)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	got, err := parseFields([]byte(converted.Fields))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, want, got)
}

func TestLegacyFieldsRead(t *testing.T) {
	item := map[string]*dynamodb.AttributeValue{
		"SessionID": {S: aws.String("session")},
		"EventIndex": {N: aws.String("1")},
		"Fields": {S: aws.String(`{"legacy":true}`)},
	}
	e, err := unmarshalEventItem(item)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	var fields map[string]interface{}
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(e.Fields), &fields))
	require.Equal(t, true, fields["legacy"])
}

func TestFieldsMapRejectsInvalidJSON(t *testing.T) {
	for _, data := range []string{``, `[]`, `null`, `{"broken":`, `{"a":1} {"b":2}`} {
		_, err := fieldsMapFromJSON([]byte(data))
		require.Error(t, err, data)
	}
}
EOF

item.text:
DynamoDB audit events now write metadata to the native `FieldsMap` attribute. Reads accept both `FieldsMap` and legacy JSON `Fields` records, so audit queries continue during migration. A distributed lock protects the batched migration; interrupted runs resume by scanning for records that still need conversion. Conversion validates that the metadata retains the same JSON content and logs progress and record errors. I also added `backend.FlagKey`.

`git diff --check` and `go test ./lib/events/dynamoevents ./lib/backend -count=1` passed. The AWS-dependent suite was skipped because its opt-in setting was absent. I completed the work directly; there were no delegations or adoptions.
